title: Free vibration + explicit/implicit cross-check
objective: Phase 7 acceptance: on a free-vibrating elastic block, the computed first natural period must match the analytical prediction within 1%; on a quasi-static problem, explicit and implicit solvers must converge to the same equilibrium within 1e-6.
scope: Free-vibration test: run an elastic block with a small initial displacement and zero force; FFT the displacement time series and compare the dominant frequency to the analytical first-mode frequency within 1%.
Cross-check test: run a quasi-static problem (slowly-applied load) with both explicit (with mass scaling) and implicit solvers; compare final displacements within 1e-6.
Mark both as `@pytest.mark.slow` since they require many time steps.
implementation_steps: Compute the analytical first-mode frequency for a fixed-fixed elastic block.
Run the explicit solver for N * T_analytical time steps with the initial displacement.
FFT the center-node displacement history and extract the peak frequency.
For the cross-check, apply a slow ramp load and run both solvers.
acceptance_criteria: Computed first-mode frequency matches analytical within 1%.
Explicit vs implicit quasi-static final displacement within 1e-6.
risks: Explicit quasi-static requires mass scaling to finish in reasonable time. Mitigation: use a scaled density ~1e6 and document the scaling in the test.
completion_notes: Free vibration: free-fixed axial bar 20x1x1 Hex8, f_1 = c/(4L), FFT peak within 1% of analytical
Cross-check: 2x2x2 Hex8, rho scaled 1e6, 4000 ramp + 16000 hold steps + 2% damping, max|u_e - u_i| < 1e-6
